per_event.why: In Y, the ship has a subtle thruster trail and banking tilt cues that follow direction changes smoothly (0.0-6.0s), whereas X only shows the static ship model.
Neither clip shows single tap shots; both clips only show charged arc shots after resting.

In Y, disarmed enemies get a distinct white ring/crosshair indicator around them and a clear metallic 'clink' sound when their weapon breaks off (e.g., Y at 0.3s, 2.0s, 5.2s), whereas in X they simply change color slightly with no clear disarm feedback (X at 2.3s, 4.1s).

In Y, charging shows a rising pitch audio cue, a pulsing ring around the ship, and a visible forward firing-arc cone showing the width/range of the charge (Y at 0.0-0.2s, 1.0-1.9s, 4.2-5.0s). X only shows the tiny 'WAIT' meter in the top-left UI and a flash on release (X at 1.9s, 3.8s).

In Y, when the charged arc hits enemies (0.2s, 1.9s, 5.1s), each hit produces a crisp impact sound, hit-sparks, and target lock rings on affected enemies. In X (2.1s, 4.0s), the arc passes through enemies with very muted visual/audio impact feedback.
Neither clip shows shots bouncing off armor.
No boss is present in either clip.
Only Clip X shows the player losing a life (at 4.1s, with a red screen border flash, explosion sound, and life pip lost in the top right). Clip Y does not show a player death.

When the wide charged shot hits multiple enemies at once in Y (e.g., 1.9s and 5.1s), individual hit markers/rings appear on each hit enemy and distinct layered impact sounds play, making it clear which enemies were affected compared to X at 2.1s and 4.0s.

clutter.issue: Bright white flash around the player ship when releasing a charged shot briefly obscures nearby pink enemy bullets.
The bright white charge-ready burst around the player ship is very large and momentarily obscures nearby enemy bullets.
Scrolling vertical road-like lane lines and yellow dots on the floor add visual noise behind small pink bullets, whereas Y has a cleaner, darker floor.

overall.why: Clip Y is much easier to read as combat because it provides a clear on-ship aiming cone and audio buildup for charged shots, distinct visual rings and sound effects when enemies are hit or disarmed, and a cleaner playfield floor with less background texture noise.
